problem.statement: Partner onboarding, first-store readiness, approval, publication and payout setup must form one governed journey with trusted platform/operator context and explicit Partner/Store ownership instead of disconnected surface-specific records and manual checks.
problem.currentWorkaround: Operators may need to reconcile partner, store, document, visit, publication and payout state across separate surfaces/services when the canonical journey is incomplete.

actors.role: Captures and maintains an assigned partner and first-store onboarding draft with governed evidence inside trusted session/assignment scope.
forbiddenActions: reassign a store owned by another partner
write financial ledger or settlement truth
select or override trusted platform/operator context

actors.role: Reads governed activation, readiness, store scope and team state for the authenticated partner business scope.
forbiddenActions: read raw payout identifiers from DSH
read another partner or store outside authorized scope

actors.role: Reviews documents/evidence, links eligible unowned stores, and applies governed activation/publication decisions through trusted operator context.
forbiddenActions: reassign a store owned by another partner
persist raw payout identifiers in DSH
read or mutate records outside trusted operator/business scope

actors.role: Discovers a store only after all applicable publication gates are satisfied.

surfaces.exclusionReason: Captain assignment and fulfillment begin in later order/dispatch journeys after store publication.

outcome.statement: A partner can be onboarded from field draft to a client-visible first store through one traceable trusted-context-aware state model, while Partner/Store business ownership is explicit and WLT exclusively owns raw payout details.
outcome.primaryMetric: percentage of submitted partner drafts reaching a governed terminal decision without manual cross-system reconciliation
guardrailMetrics: zero cross-scope partner, store, document, visit or audit reads/writes
zero stores reassigned between partners outside an explicit transfer journey
zero raw payout account identifiers returned by DSH
zero client-visible stores failing any publication gate
zero duplicate transition audit events for identical retries
outcome.baselineState: The capability must eliminate disconnected readiness checks, weak retry identity, raw payout data in DSH and ambiguous trusted-context/business-scope ownership.
outcome.targetState: Every mutation is trusted-context derived, Partner/Store scoped, authorization-scoped, concurrency-safe, idempotent, audited and readable on required surfaces.
outcome.observationWindow: one complete onboarding cycle plus the monitoring period defined by the active release/operations profile

criteria: Platform/operator context is derived only from trusted Identity/server-side context; browser headers, query parameters and request bodies cannot select or override it.
Requests requiring trusted context fail closed when it is absent and do not reach partner persistence.
Partner lists, details, documents, visits, stores, assignments/scopes, transitions and audit records are read/mutated only within trusted context plus object/business authorization.
Cross-scope partner/store identifiers do not disclose ownership details.
Business/legal identity uniqueness follows the current contract without conflating Partner/Store with platform isolation context.
Field agents can create, resume, save and submit only assigned/authorized onboarding drafts.
Submission is blocked until the current required legal, first-store and WLT payout-reference prerequisites are complete.
Required documents/evidence satisfy the current independent review/approval policy before activation.
Partner activation requires the current evidence-bearing field/readiness prerequisites.
Client publication requires every applicable partner/store/catalog/marketing/serviceability gate.
A store already owned by one partner cannot be linked to another through the generic onboarding link operation.
Identical transition and payout retries replay the original result; payload changes under the same idempotency identity are rejected.
DSH persists/returns only WLT payout references or masked compatibility values allowed by the current contract.
Partner and control-panel surfaces read back committed activation/readiness state.
failureStates: trusted context selected from client-controlled input
raw payout data stored or returned by DSH
surface reports success before committed readback
requiredChecks: PostgreSQL migration and trusted-context/business-scope isolation tests
visual and RTL review when applicable

business: Every partner/onboarding child record belongs to the trusted platform/operator context and explicit Partner/Store business scope required by the current model.
One partner may own multiple stores, but one store has at most one onboarding owner unless an explicit transfer model says otherwise.
Control-panel approval is distinct from field evidence capture.
WLT is the sole owner of raw payout destination data.
Client visibility is a store publication outcome, not merely a partner status label.
Every material transition records the actor/trusted context/business scope/correlation/retry/audit data required by current contracts.
negative: Client-controlled input cannot select trusted platform/operator context.
Missing required trusted context cannot silently fall back inside partner handlers.
One Partner/Store scope cannot enumerate, read, link, mutate or infer another unauthorized business scope.
A field agent cannot approve their own evidence where separation is required.
A partner cannot bypass store publication gates.
A store cannot be reassigned by the generic link operation.
DSH cannot persist raw payout account data after binding a WLT reference.
A stale version cannot mutate partner state.
A reused idempotency key cannot represent a different payload.
A store failing any applicable publication gate cannot appear to clients.

execution.appetite: Close the applicable vertical slices of the current onboarding/publication journey and stop at the highest evidence-backed decision without implying merge/release/production authority.
fixedConstraints: Repository truth is the current user-named work branch and resolved immutable candidate SHA.
DSH owns operational Partner/Store state; WLT owns payout/financial truth.
Trusted platform/operator context is server-derived and never accepted from client-controlled input.
No store reassignment through the generic onboarding link route.
No raw payout identifiers persisted or returned by DSH.
No downstream journey is represented as closed while a required onboarding/publication dependency remains open.
variableScope: non-breaking compatibility mappings for masked payout fields
forbiddenScope: fabricated runtime, QA, security, finance or visual evidence
execution.forecastRange: one governed journey implementation and evidence cycle
unknowns: same-commit runtime and visual evidence until executed
historical raw payout rows without a WLT reference may require a separately verified forward migration before production cleanup
